The Mountain Maidu are the northeastern branch of the Maidu people of California, living in the high valleys of the northern Sierra Nevada, such as Indian Valley, American Valley and Big Meadows, south of Lassen Peak. Their kin to the west were the Konkow and to the south the Nisenan.

They lived in villages in the mountain meadows, gathering acorns and seeds, fishing and hunting deer, and moved higher in summer. Their eastern neighbours were the Northern Paiute. The Gold Rush brought miners into their valleys from 1850, followed by ranchers and loggers. In 1914 a dam flooded Big Meadows to make Lake Almanor, covering many old village sites. Today the Mountain Maidu live in Plumas and Lassen counties.
